"There are also young girls saying that they want to get into law enforcement, and they're inspired by my story. And then, I serve my community in Westborough every single day in my capacity as a police officer, but I also get to serve my community in the role as Miss Massachusetts." "Those two things are what is so important about the Miss America opportunity," Mercier said. "Yes, we get to dress up. Yes, we get to wear pretty gowns and look beautiful. But, women's empowerment and service are the core. And if you look at it like that, you can see and draw a lot of parallels between Miss America and between my role as Officer Mercier." articles.title: Trump pardons Jay-Z associate Emory Jones after federal drug conviction
articles.summary: Alice Marie Johnson revealed Trump granted clemency to 30 individuals, including Emory Jones, a Roc Nation executive and Jay-Z's longtime associate.
articles.body: Emory Jones, longtime friend and business associate of Jay-Z, has been granted a pardon by President Donald Trump. Jones, who is now an executive in Jay-Z's Roc Nation, was sentenced to nearly 16 years in 2000 on federal drug charges. Thanks in part to a letter from the hip-hop mogul, his sentence was reduced by 37 months, but now, Trump has given him a completely clean slate. The news was shared this week by Alice Marie Johnson, who was pardoned by Trump in 2020 after being sentenced to life in prison on a nonviolent drug charge in 1996. She now works with the White House as the "pardon czar." JELLY ROLL GRANTED PARDON BY TENNESSEE GOVERNOR IN CHRISTMAS SEASON CLEMENCY DECISION "Yesterday was a powerful day for second chances," Johnson wrote on Instagram. "I am deeply grateful to President @realdonaldtrump for granting clemency and pardons to 30 deserving individuals whose cases we carefully reviewed and brought forward—and to the White House Counsel team, led by Will Scharf, for the hard work behind these decisions." She added, "Among them is Emory Jones, who served nearly 16 years in federal prison and came home determined to build a different life. Today he is an entrepreneur and creative leader whose journey reminds us how much people can grow—and how much good they can still do." TODD CHRISLEY RECALLS EMOTIONAL PHONE CALL WITH DAUGHTER SAVANNAH AFTER CONTROVERSIAL TRUMP PARDON In 1999, Jones pleaded guilty to a charge of conspiracy to distribute cocaine. The following year, he was sentenced to 188 months, nearly 16 years, in prison, with five years supervised release. Jones' legal team submitted a request for a reduction of his sentence in 2009, and as part of their request, they submitted a series of letters from people familiar with Jones, including Jay-Z. In a letter to the judge, Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, wrote that he'd be offering Jones an executive assistant job with Roc Apparel Group upon his release, with a starting salary of $50,000. "It is my strong desire to have Mr. Jones fill this position. I have known Mr. Jones for 15 years. I believe his attributes, including intelligence, interpersonal skills and solid work ethic will be a significant asset for my organization." In another letter, Jones himself wrote about his conviction, saying, "Of all the excuses that I could have attributed my demise to, I chose not to use a single one. Excuses are tools of the incompetent and only build monuments to nothingness." Nothing monetary because you can't put a price on love and support. However, you do owe them the privilege and opportunity to see you do something extremely positive with your life." articles.title: 'Shah Rukh Khan said I'm a Pathaan, just shoot me if you want,' Sanjay Gupta recalled how the superstar refused to bow down to underworld threats
articles.summary: Shah Rukh Khan’s rise to superstardom coincided with a period when Mumbai’s underworld had a strong and often intimidating presence in Bollywood. Acto.
articles.body: Shah Rukh Khan’s rise to superstardom coincided with a period when Mumbai’s underworld had a strong and often intimidating presence in Bollywood. Actors, filmmakers and producers were sometimes subjected to threats and pressure, and Shah Rukh too found himself on the radar of gangsters. Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has now recalled how the actor refused to be intimidated and stood his ground despite the risks involved.Gupta said Shah Rukh responded to the threats in unusually defiant fashion. According to the filmmaker, the actor made it clear that he would not allow anyone to dictate the films or shows he worked on.He said on Hussain Zaidi's podcast, "The only guy in the film industry, Shah Rukh Khan, when he was threatened, he said, ‘I will never do the film or show, I am a Pathaan, just shoot me if you want’. I am not scared of you, but I will not work with you and not do shows for you. He actually earned their respect. They also must have felt that there’s at least one person…”Despite his bold stance, the threats were serious enough for Shah Rukh to remain under police and security protection for around three years.The actor had previously opened up about the dangers he faced during the 1990s in an interview with comedian and actor Ruby Wax. Recalling how the underworld allegedly operated, Shah Rukh explained the pressure stars could face when they refused to cooperate.“They would set up a system, and they would say you do it. I may not have succumbed to it, but then they shoot you. So, sometimes it’s nice to do a film,” he said.Wax then sought clarification, asking, “You’re seriously saying someone calls you and says be in my film or I’ll blow your head off?”Shah Rukh confirmed that the reality was even more disturbing than Wax’s description.“Not as nicely as you’re saying it.” When asked whether he had personally received death threats, the actor did not hesitate.“Oh yes, on many occasions… I had a lot of security for three years.Shah Rukh’s willingness to confront threats was also recalled by filmmaker Karan Johar in his autobiography An Unsuitable Boy. Johar described an incident in which he himself faced pressure from the underworld around the release of Kuch Kuch Hota Hai.According to Johar, Shah Rukh refused to let the situation intimidate either of them. He wrote, “Shah Rukh said, ‘What nonsense!’ He went inside and dragged me out. He said, ‘I’m standing here in front of you. Let’s see who shoots you. I’m standing right here.’”Johar further recalled Shah Rukh reassuring his mother and making it clear that he would stand by his friend.“I’m a Pathan. Nothing can happen to me and nothing will happen to your son. He’s like my brother. Nothing’s gonna happen.”The relationship between Mumbai’s film industry and the underworld was not a new phenomenon, but the nexus became increasingly visible during the late 1980s and 1990s. Allegations involving illegal financing, interference in film projects and threats against industry figures brought the issue into sharper focus.The 1997 killing of music baron Gulshan Kumar became one of the most high-profile incidents highlighting the risks associated with the alleged nexus. The issue resurfaced prominently in 2001 with the Chori Chori Chupke Chupke case, which led to the arrest of financier Bharat Shah and producer Nazim Rizvi over alleged links to gangster Chhota Shakeel.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: CD sales are booming as physical media continues its resurgence
articles.summary: CD sales are booming, and vinyl continues its resurgence, but that doesn’t mean people are abandoning streaming.
articles.body: According to the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), CD sales exploded in the first half of 2026. A new report from the organization says 17.5 million CDs were sold in the first six months of the year, up from just 12 million during the same period in 2025. That’s a jump of 45.7 percent, and 58.6 percent in dollars, which reached $171.1 million. What makes this all the more shocking is that CD sales actually shrank 22 percent from 2024 to 2025. The RIAA isn’t the only one to notice the boom in CD sales. In July, research firm Luminate released a report saying that 16.3 million units were sold in the first half of 2026. It suggested that much of that increase was due to special editions from K-Pop acts like BTS and that Gen Z and millennials were treating them mostly as collectibles, saying that only about half of buyers actually owned a CD player. Vinyl continued its resurgence as well, with the number of units sold climbing by nearly 21 percent from last year to 26.5 million. “Other physical” media, which includes CD singles, DVDs, cassettes, SACD, DVD-Audio… basically anything besides “standard vinyl and CD albums,” also surged by over 73 percent, to 1.6 million units. Despite the increased interest in physical media and the ongoing iPod revival, people are not leaving streaming in droves. Streaming revenue grew by 4.7 percent to $4.9 billion — dwarfing all physical media combined. [Image: Those are some big jumps in sales.

articles.title: Rick Moranis, Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan among stars who left fame behind before returning to Hollywood
articles.summary: From Rick Moranis to Cameron Diaz and Lindsay Lohan, these Hollywood stars walked away from fame and made remarkable comebacks years later on screen.
articles.body: Rick Moranis is stepping back into the spotlight after decades away from Hollywood, joining a growing list of stars who left fame behind and later returned. The 71-year-old actor is taking on his first live-action part in nearly 30 years after walking away from the entertainment industry at the height of his career following a family tragedy. Now, Moranis is reprising his role as Lord Dark Helmet in "Spaceballs: The New One," the long-awaited sequel to Mel Brooks' 1987 cult classic science-fiction comedy movie "Spaceballs." 'DEADPOOL' STAR ROB DELANEY REVEALS HOW LOSING 2-YEAR-OLD SON CHANGED HIS APPROACH TO FAME In July, Moranis made a rare public appearance to promote the sequel at San Diego Comic-Con, where he received a standing ovation when he appeared on stage wearing his character's signature massive black helmet. Moranis participated in a panel discussion alongside co-stars Daphne Zuniga, Josh Gad, Keke Palmer and Lewis Pullman as well as director Josh Greenbaum and screenwriters Benji Samit and Dan Hernandez. Zuniga is reprising her role as Princess Vespa while other original stars who returned for the sequel include George Wyner as Colonel Sandurz, Bill Pullman as Lone Starr and Brooks as Yogurt. During the panel, Moranis revealed what finally brought him back in front of the camera after his decades-long hiatus. "This came along right at the right time, and I started talking to these folks and hearing who was going to be in it," Moranis said, via People. "I spoke to Josh Greenbaum and I heard that Bill Pullman was coming back and that Lewis was going to be in it too, and it just felt like this is it. It’s time and — yes. I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made." Moranis became one of Hollywood's most recognizable comedy stars in the 1980s and 1990s after starring in a string of hit movies including "Spaceballs," "Ghostbusters," "Little Shop of Horrors," "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids," "Parenthood," "My Blue Heaven" and "The Flintstones." However, after his wife, costume designer Ann Belsky, died in 1991 following a battle with breast cancer, Moranis stepped away from show business to focus on raising their two children, daughter Rachel and son Mitchell. He last appeared on-screen in 1997's "Honey, We Shrunk Ourselves," the third installment in the "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids" movie series. During a 2015 interview with the Hollywood Reporter, Moranis reflected on his decision to prioritize his family over his career. "I was working with really interesting people, wonderful people," he said. "I went from that to being at home with a couple of little kids, which is a very different lifestyle. But it was important to me. I have absolutely no regrets whatsoever. My life is wonderful." Moranis also clarified that he had not officially retired from acting, telling the outlet, "I took a break, which turned into a longer break." "But I’m interested in anything that I would find interesting," he continued. "I still get the occasional query about a film or television role and as soon as one comes along that piques my interest, I'll probably do it." MATT DAMON SAYS HOLLYWOOD'S 'RUTHLESS' NATURE HAS TAKEN HIM AWAY FROM FATHERHOOD MORE THAN HE'D LIKE "I’m happy with the things I said yes to, and I’m very happy with the many things I’ve said no to," Moranis added. "Yes, I am picky, and I’ll continue to be picky. Picky has worked for me." Though Moranis left live-action films behind for many years, he continued working occasionally as a voice actor. He first dipped his toe back into the movie business in 2001, voicing two characters in "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer & the Island of Misfit Toys." Some of his other voice-acting gigs include "Brother Bear," "The Animated Adventures of Bob & Doug McKenzie," and the voice of Dark Helmet in "The Goldbergs." During his appearance at Comic-Con, Moranis once again set the record straight regarding the perception that he had retired as he revealed that he and Brooks had long discussed making a follow-up to "Spaceballs." "Actually, I started talking to Mel about the sequel in 1989," he said. "We kept talking about it." "I really wasn’t retired; I was just negotiating," Moranis joked. STOCKARD CHANNING HITS FIRST RED CARPET IN 2 YEARS AFTER SAYING SHE'S A 'RECLUSE' While Moranis’ return has drawn renewed attention due to his decades-long absence, other stars have also taken long breaks from Hollywood before making high-profile comebacks. Here's a look at several celebrities who stepped away from the spotlight for years before finding their way back to the screen. Cameron Diaz Cameron Diaz was one of Hollywood’s most bankable stars when she quietly stepped away from acting in 2014. Diaz made her breakthrough in 1994's "The Mask" and went on to star in a series of hit films including "There’s Something About Mary," "My Best Friend's Wedding," "Charlie's Angels," "My Sister's Keeper," "Shrek" and "The Other Woman," among others. After starring in 2014's "Annie," Diaz walked away from show business to focus on building a life with husband Benji Madden. "It felt like the right thing for me to reclaim my own life, and I just really didn't care about anything else," the actress said during a 2025 appearance at Fortune's Most Powerful Women Summit, according to E! News. "Nobody's opinion, nobody's success, no one's offer, no one's anything could change my mind about my decision of taking care of myself and building the life that I really wanted to have. I think it really comes to what are you passionate about? For me, it was to build my family." During her break, Diaz welcomed daughter Raddix, 6, and son Cardinal, 2, with Madden and launched her Avaline wine brand. The couple's third child, son Nautus, was born in May. After a decade away from movies, Diaz returned to the screen in Netflix’s 2025 action comedy "Back in Action," starring opposite Jamie Foxx. She has since lined up other projects including Netflix’s "Bad Day," Apple TV+’s "Outcome" and "Shrek 5," in which she will reprise her voice role as Princess Fiona. Lindsay Lohan Lindsay Lohan’s comeback followed years of intense public scrutiny and a long stretch away from major studio films. Lohan became one of Hollywood’s biggest young stars after breaking out in "The Parent Trap" and later leading hits including "Freaky Friday," "Mean Girls" and "Herbie: Fully Loaded." However, Lohan's promising career was derailed by multiple box-office flops and a string of highly-publicized legal problems and substance abuse issues. After years of tabloid attention and personal struggles, Lohan left the United States in 2014 and eventually relocated full-time to Dubai, spending much of the next decade outside the Hollywood spotlight. She told Emirates Woman in 2018 that moving to Dubai afforded her "a fresh start." Lohan began rebuilding her acting career with Netflix’s 2022 holiday movie "Falling for Christmas," followed by more streaming projects and a major return to one of her signature roles in "Freakier Friday." During a 2025 interview with The Sunday Times, Lohan said she stepped away because she had lost her excitement for making movies and wanted "a more private life, a real life," before returning once she felt "that itch again." Lohan will next be seen in Hulu’s "Count My Lies," a limited series in which she stars opposite Shailene Woodley and Kit Harington. Ke Huy Quan Ke Huy Quan’s Hollywood disappearance ended with one of the industry’s most celebrated comeback stories. Quan became a child star after playing Short Round opposite Harrison Ford in 1984’s "Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom" and Data in 1985’s "The Goonies." However, Ke only landed a few minor TV and film roles after his early fame and found himself being offered stereotypical parts geared toward Asians. During a 2023 interview with People, Quan said that he made the "very difficult decision" to walk away from acting in the early 2000s. He then spent years working behind the camera as a stunt coordinator and assistant director. However, he recalled that after seeing 2018’s "Crazy Rich Asians", he was inspired to revisit his first love. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "I was happy working behind the camera, but I had serious FOMO (fear of missing out)," Ke told the outlet. "I wanted to be up there with my fellow Asian actors." After roughly two decades away from acting, Quan returned in 2022’s "Everything Everywhere All at Once," a role that earned him the Academy Award for best supporting actor. In his emotional Oscars speech, Quan reflected on his unlikely journey, saying, "Dreams are something you have to believe in. I almost gave up on mine." Daniel Day-Lewis Daniel Day-Lewis has stepped away from Hollywood more than once, but his latest return marked the end of what many believed was a permanent retirement. Known for his intensely selective approach to roles, Day-Lewis has previously taken long breaks throughout his career. After starring in 1997’s "The Boxer," Day-Lewis retreated from acting and spent several years in Italy learning shoemaking before returning in Martin Scorsese’s 2002 film "Gangs of New York." The three-time Oscar winner announced he was retiring from acting after starring in 2017’s "Phantom Thread." At the time, his representative said, "Daniel Day-Lewis will no longer be working as an actor. He is immensely grateful to all of his collaborators and audiences over the many years. This is a private decision and neither he nor his representatives will make any further comment on this subject." Eight years later, his son, Ronan Day-Lewis, persuaded him to co-write and star in the 2025 drama "Anemone." Day-Lewis later pushed back on the idea that he ever meant to permanently retire. In a 2025 Rolling Stone interview, Day-Lewis said he "never intended to retire, really," and called his earlier retirement announcement "grandiose gibberish." He explained that he still loved the work, but struggled with the lifestyle around filmmaking and felt "hollowed out" after "Phantom Thread." He said returning for "Anemone" was largely about working with Ronan, who directed the film. Day-Lewis said that collaboration brought the spark back, saying, "working with Ro, that furnace just lit up." Renée Zellweger Renée Zellweger stepped away from Hollywood after years of working at a relentless pace. Zellweger became one of the most prominent actresses of the late 1990s and 2000s with roles in the hit movies "Jerry Maguire," "Bridget Jones’s Diary," "Chicago," "Cold Mountain" and "Cinderella Man." But after 2010’s "My Own Love Song," Zellweger took a six-year break from acting. During a 2025 interview with British Vogue, Zellweger explained why she decided to pause her career. "I was sick of the sound of my own voice. When I was working, I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, listen to you. Are you sad again, Renée? Oh, is this your mad voice?’ It was a regurgitation of the same emotional experiences," she said. Zellweger told the outlet that her hiatus from acting enabled her to pursue other projects and embrace a healthier lifestyle. "I built a house, rescued a pair of older doggies, created a partnership that led to a production company, advocated for and fundraised with a sick friend, and spent a lot of time with family and godchildren and driving across the country with the dogs. I got healthy." Zellweger returned in 2016 with the hit sequel "Bridget Jones’s Baby." She went on to earn some of the strongest reviews of her career for playing Judy Garland in 2019’s "Judy" and her performance earned her the Academy Award for best actress. Zellweger previously won the best supporting actress Oscar for her performance in "Cold Mountain." Macaulay Culkin Macaulay Culkin walked away from Hollywood after becoming one of the most famous child stars in the world. Culkin shot to superstardom as Kevin McCallister in 1990’s "Home Alone" and its 1992 sequel, "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York." He went on to star in hit films including "My Girl," "The Good Son" and "Richie Rich." He returned nine years later with "Party Monster" and has continued accepting occasional projects on his own terms, including roles in "Saved!," "American Horror Story: Double Feature" and "The Righteous Gemstones." Pamela Anderson Pamela Anderson’s return to the spotlight has become one of Hollywood’s more unexpected late-career reinventions. Anderson became a global sex symbol in the 1990s through "Baywatch," Playboy and years of tabloid attention that often overshadowed her acting ambitions. After decades of being defined by her image and personal life, she retreated to Vancouver Island, embraced a quieter lifestyle and began reassessing the public persona that had followed her for much of her career. articles.title: Spencer Pratt rips George Clooney's 'woke scold lecture' after Amal's lavish Venice look
articles.summary: Spencer Pratt calls out George Clooney and Amal Clooney over Venice Film Festival glamour, saying he will never tolerate a "woke scold lecture" from the couple.
articles.body: Spencer Pratt is taking aim at George Clooney. The former reality star, who delved into politics this year with a run for mayor of Los Angeles, pulled no punches when he took to social media Friday to criticize Clooney and his wife, Amal. "$500M net worth George Clooney could’ve permanently housed 8 homeless people for the rest of their lives with the money he spent on a single-use dress for his wife at a 4 hour event," Pratt claimed on X. SPENCER PRATT'S UNEXPECTED POLITICAL RISE FROM MTV VILLAIN TO KAREN BASS' CHALLENGER He added, "I will never tolerate a woke scold lecture from these people. Just be an ostentatious celebrity and own it." Along with his post, he shared a Page Six article detailing a look Amal wore to the Venice Film Festival, where the Clooneys have been spotted several times this week. According to the outlet, she wore a custom look by Haider Ackermann for Tom Ford, as well as a pair of earrings from Cartier that cost $149,000 and a Cartier diamond bracelet that runs for $225,000. "We’re at a moment in time that’s unfortunate… that’s an understatement. I do believe that we’re going to get through all of this. I’m old enough to have been through 1968 in the States when every city in the United States was set on fire, and we lost Martin Luther King and Bobby Kennedy in the same year. There was tons of violence. The capital was surrounded with tanks. We’ve had some other difficult times, but this is one of them." articles.title: ‘Evil Dead’ star Bruce Campbell says he has five years to live after cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Actor Bruce Campbell said he has five years to live amid treatment for cancer.
articles.body: Actor Bruce Campbell said he has five years to live amid treatment for cancer. Speaking on an episode of “The Adam Carolla Show” released Thursday, the actor — best known for his roles in “The Evil Dead” horror franchise — said he has “give or take” five years left. “I’ve decided though, pretty specifically, to live with it, not die from it,” he said. “The cancer rabbit hole is enormous. You can go into focus groups of 10,000 guys who have exactly what you have. I won’t touch it with a 10-foot pole.” Campbell, 67, declined to say what type of cancer he has. He announced his diagnosis in March, saying he had a “treatable” but not “curable” type of cancer. “I apologize if that’s a shock — it was to me too,” he wrote in a post on X at the time. “The good news is, I’m not gonna go into any more detail. I’m posting this, because professionally, a few things will have to change — appearances and cons and work in general need to take a back seat to treatment.” Campbell appeared on the podcast to promote “Ernie & Emma,” an independent film he wrote, directed, produced and stars in. “I’m moving on. I got a movie to promote. And when I promote this movie, I have nothing. I’m free and clear when I promote this movie mentally,” he said. “You have to make this decision of, ‘Well, OK, but do I have to stop everything that I’m doing because of this?’ Well, no.” “It’s not just, you don’t die for cancer,” he added. “You die from what cancer does to you.”

articles.title: Brooke Hogan threatens to expose family receipts in 'final warning'
articles.summary: Brooke Hogan threatened to release screenshots after Linda Hogan accused her of tossing the family aside, escalating their public estrangement.
articles.body: Brooke Hogan is warning her family that she has receipts, and she's prepared to use them. The 38-year-old daughter of late wrestling legend fired back after her mother, Linda Hogan, publicly lamented their yearslong estrangement and accused Brooke of tossing her family aside "like trash." "This 👌 close to breaking out some screenshots – which are ONE of the many reasons WHY," Brooke wrote over a screenshot of her mother's Facebook post from August 30 shared to her Instagram Story. BROOKE HOGAN SAYS ‘I COULD HAVE SAVED YOU’ IN HAUNTING REGRET AFTER HULK HOGAN’S DEATH "I don't take CONSTANTLY dragging my name through the mud lightly," she continued. "The selective amnesia isn't gonna work." Brooke ended the message with two words: "Final warning." The latest flare-up came after Linda shared old family photos on Facebook while expressing her frustration over her fractured relationship with her daughter. "I posted these wonderful photos of Brooke my daughter with me and my ex-husband her father and my mom and dad and really .. the whole family ! Brooke is loved," Linda wrote. "We feel hurt every day that she just tosses us aside .... like trash," she continued. "I want to make sure she remembers how it really was .. and can really see how much she was adored and loved." Brooke's response suggested she remembers their family history differently and is prepared to make private communications public if the criticism continues. The mother and daughter's latest exchange is another chapter in a family fracture that has played out publicly for years. The show followed the wrestling superstar and his family while also documenting Brooke's budding music career and her father's protective approach to his teenage daughter. Their divorce was finalized in 2009. Years later, Brooke became estranged from both parents, but she has made clear that her reasons for cutting contact with her mother were separate from the issues she had with her father. Brooke addressed the family rift directly in a lengthy Instagram statement on March 27, 2025, insisting she had not chosen one parent over the other. "No contact with my mom has nothing to do with my dad, and no contact with my father has nothing to do with my mother," Brooke wrote. "I have completely separate reasons for going no contact with each of my parents." HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED In the same statement, Brooke made serious allegations about her childhood and family relationships. "I have been EXTREMELY verbally and mentally abused since childhood," she alleged. "Sadly, it would frequently turn physical. And sometimes it's not by the person you would assume, abuse comes in all shapes and sizes." Brooke did not identify a specific person in that portion of her statement. She also claimed she had been put in the position of publicly defending behavior within her family before eventually questioning what she had been told. "I've been asked to defend poor behavior to the public and have done so out of love. Only to find I was misinformed, manipulated, and lied to," she wrote. "I longed for a normal family, but it never came to fruition. I've repeatedly held my hand out to help them, only to have them pull me into the darkness with them." She continued, "I've set boundaries that were not respected, which turned into a 'no contact' situation." Her comments came after Linda publicly discussed the family's troubles in March 2025, reigniting attention around their strained relationship. The conflict marked a dramatic departure from the image viewers were introduced to two decades earlier on "Hogan Knows Best." Brooke was a teenager when the series premiered, with the show following her budding music career, dating life and her father's famously protective parenting. WWE LEGEND HULK HOGAN'S DEATH REPORT RELEASED In the years that followed, the family relationships viewers once watched on television became increasingly strained, with some of those disputes eventually playing out in public. Her relationship with her father received renewed attention following his death on July 24, 2025. Hulk, born Terry Bollea, died at age 71 after being hospitalized for cardiac arrest. Hulk was survived by Brooke and Nick, whom he shared with Linda, as well as his wife, Sky Daily. Despite being estranged from her father when he died, Brooke made clear in an April interview with Fox News Digital that her love for him had never disappeared. "I’m honest with him now, and I talk to him all the time, even if that seems like I’m a cuckoo bird," she told Fox News Digital. "If he showed up today, I would just be like, ‘I love you so much, and I wish you would have just let me in.’" Brooke also offered rare insight into why their relationship had become strained before his death. "[It's] tough because, obviously, my dad and I weren't really speaking prior to his death — not because I didn't love him… it's that he had become a little bit calloused in the direction he was going in his life and the people he was surrounding himself with," she said. And it's kind of like, you can try to save somebody and if they don't want to be saved… it's a tough position to be in." Her comments to Fox News Digital echoed what Brooke had emphasized in her March 2025 statement: distancing herself from her father did not mean she had sided with her mother, or vice versa. articles.title: Jeff Foxworthy reveals how 'redneck' insult inspired decades of comedy
articles.summary: Jeff Foxworthy reveals why he brought back his iconic "redneck" jokes after 20 years for his Fox Nation special "The Joke's on Me" streaming now.
articles.body: Jeff Foxworthy turned an insult into a compliment when someone criticized where he came from. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 67-year-old actor and comedian discussed his new stand-up special, "The Joke's on Me," and recalled the time someone called him a "redneck," and how he turned what was meant to be an insult into a compliment. He explained that "one of the nicest compliments" someone once gave him was commending his ability to turn what "was supposed to be an insult...into a badge of honor." "I said, 'Well, that's cool, because when people get offended, they act like if you gave rednecks a billion dollars, they wouldn't be rednecks,'" he said. "I said they would still be rednecks. They would just have bigger boats, bigger truck. I mean, more things to shoot at. They're happy with who they are. And I've always got asked, ‘How do you come up with that?’ And I'm like. There's no research going on. It's my family and my friend group that trust me." DAVE CHAPPELLE SAYS HE’S CONSIDERING REVISITING ‘CHAPPELLE’S SHOW’ DECADES AFTER WALKING AWAY Foxworthy first began telling jokes about rednecks in the late '80s, and found them to be extremely successful, so he continued telling them, even closing his 1990 special with one. He explained that "they were easy to remember" and said they would always "get a laugh." After telling the jokes on stage for a while, he "thought, well people are tired of this," and stopped telling them, adding, "The last time I did them onstage was during the Blue Collar Comedy Tour" in 2003. WATCH: Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up. After more than 20 years of staying away from the jokes, Foxworthy felt like it was time to bring them back. He recalled telling the crowd, "I hadn't done these in 20 years, but I'm thinking about for this special, bringing them back." "I said that because when I said that if you've ever peed in the pool, the entire audience went, 'You might be a redneck.' And I went, 'Oh, wow, this stuck to people's bones, you know?'" he said. "And I say, well, what if I did some to close, if that was my first special, and all these years later, this is my last. It kind of seemed like a nice little way to put a bow on it." He then went back and looked at all the redneck jokes he had written over the years, "and pulled out a bunch of them" to try at his next gig at a comedy club. "It was like, I never stopped doing them," he said. "It was like going back 35 years, which was really cool for me. It's like one of your babies. You bring it back out and people go, 'Oh, we still love it.'" WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy explains why he stopped telling 'redneck' jokes Foxworthy's latest comedy special, "The Joke's on Me" began streaming on Fox Nation in June. Unlike other comedy specials, this one gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at the joke writing process that goes into creating a special. The comedian told Fox News Digital he was inspired to create the unique special after watching a documentary about the Beatles and realizing that "seeing the process didn't take anything away from the finished product," but rather made it better "because you saw the struggle that went into creating that." Because one of the things that still fascinates me after over 40 years about stand-up is I still don't know what people are gonna laugh at," he said. And so I wanted to show that. And Fox Nation was the first place that ever said, 'Okay, we'll do it.'" articles.title: Christie Brinkley shares how she keeps her three adult children coming home
articles.summary: Christie Brinkley reveals how she keeps all three adult children coming home and why losing both parents deepened her devotion to family time.
articles.body: Christie Brinkley never really had to face an empty nest. The actress and supermodel stars opposite Steve Guttenberg in "American Summer," a feel-good tribute to simpler times and family connections. The 72-year-old told Fox News Digital that those themes aren't just on-screen — they're values she's embraced in her own life, creating a home her three adult children can still return to. The movie, which hit theaters Sept. 4, follows Guttenberg's character as he looks back on a formative childhood summer filled with baseball, first love and the disappearance of his U.S. Army father overseas. CHRISTIE BRINKLEY HAS FANS MISTAKING SUPERMODEL FOR DAUGHTER IN NEW PHOTOS "I have always been all about family, so I have built my life in a way that my kids ... I want them independent," Brinkley said. "I want them out there living, doing whatever, but they always tend to come home on weekends, holidays. We all really are big on being together, and I love that." "It's funny because a lot of moms on Instagram will ask me, 'How do you get your kids to come home so often? Mine are off and about,'" the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl shared. "And I think it's just to always let them know they're always welcome back. They can bring their friends, that kind of thing." The supermodel is often photographed alongside her three grown children — Alexa Ray Joel, 40, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook, 31, and Sailor Brinkley-Cook, 28 — whether they're walking red carpets or stepping out in coordinated looks. Brinkley said their close bond didn't happen by accident but was rooted in the example set by her own parents. WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY SHARES SECRET TO KEEPING HER FAMILY CLOSE After losing both of her parents less than two months apart in 2012, Brinkley said she no longer takes family time for granted. Her father, Don Brinkley, died July 14, followed by her mother, Marge Brinkley, on Sept. 9. "I have always cherished my family time," Brinkley said. "And I think once you lose both of your parents, it becomes more precious because you know that there is a finite time to it. And right now, our family's smaller because I don't have my mom and dad." Brinkley became visibly emotional before saying, "I always get choked up whenever I talk about them." Guttenberg is no stranger to Brinkley's heartbreak. He became a caregiver for his father, Stanley Guttenberg, after he developed kidney failure, eventually training to help administer dialysis at home. "I remember you telling me about your mom and dad, Christie, that you had a little house on your property, and they lived near you, right?" Guttenberg said. "Isn't that wonderful? How lucky you were and are to have them right there. It's priceless, right? ... The greatest thing in the world." "The best," Brinkley replied. "My parents were always, always so ready to be there for me. Good times, bad times, they were always there, and they always made an effort to be a family. And I think it's so important, and it has given me my happiest moments." She shared that Alexa Ray was preparing for a concert that night, while Jack planned to attend the premiere of "American Summer" alongside her. For Brinkley, the movie's message extends beyond the screen. She believes audiences are craving stories that celebrate family. "... People want to put down their phone and speak to another human face to face," she said. "... This [story] takes us back before there were cell phones. And I think that we're going to find people now putting down their cell phones more often and just connecting with loved ones. And that human connection, nothing can replace it. I find that whenever I light a little bonfire in the backyard or at the beach, I always say, 'This is it. This is free. This is simple. And you know what? This is as good as it gets.'" "Just to be able to sit there by the crackling of the fire, the moon coming up, the stars sparkling, the birds chirping, the crickets coming on, the fireflies lighting — that's it," she continued. "That's the best. Slowing down the speed of life, human connections ... I think those are things that we all want to feel again and again." "It's better than any Ferrari," Guttenberg said. Brinkley's love of simple pleasures doesn't stop with family gatherings. She's also an avid birdwatcher — a hobby she believes is making a comeback as more people look to unplug.
